banner.title: The specialists round - Hettlestad's Healers (folios 22-23) and Mumper's Scribes (folios 23, 25)
banner.provenance: Pinned from The Dragon Vol. 1 No. 3 (October 1976): folios 22-23, C. Hettlestad's Healers - the rapid-repair class with its 15-each prerequisites, the 8-sided hit dice, the level-unlock abilities at 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th and 20th, and the twenty-five-level ladder with its spell-progression grid; folios 23 and 25, David Mumper's Scribes - the rare and expensive specialists who alone may transcribe magical writing, with the find and leave chances, the hire rates, the six-grade ability ladder with its mistake and insanity percents, and the alignment bands by vocation. The editor's caution rides: none of this is official, and the alchemist precedent holds - specialists are non-player-character recommended.
banner.sentinel: The variant-layer doctrine holds: Dragon ink is never core 1e canon. The Healer's printed hit-dice forms 10+N are CONVERTED to base-plus-bonus columns and the spell-grid dashes CONVERTED to zeros, both conversions noted, never silent; the Scribe alignment block garbles in OCR and pins AS SCANNED with the clerical vocation's missing neutral band carried as the sentinel 9; the mistake percent pairs read as within-abilities over above-abilities and pin as scanned. The Healer and Scribe ride the variant layer against the engine's canon class frame, never a rewrite.

audit_comment: THE SPECIALISTS ROUND - round B of the issue-3 walk. Hettlestad's Healer: the prerequisites (15 each in intelligence, wisdom and dexterity, lawful or neutral only, a chaotic becoming a mere fighter), no armor or shield, any weapons and magical items, the books that only hurt; the level-unlock abilities - detect molds and slimes at 40 feet at 4th, determine potions at 8th, read magical and clerical scrolls at 12th, four 1st-level magic-user spells at 16th, four 2nd-level at 20th; the twenty-five-level ladder (Apprentice through Doctor 25th) with the 8-sided hit dice split from the printed 10+N forms and the seven-column spell-progression grid, the dashes converted to zeros; the racial caps - Medic 10th for Dwarves, Doctor 14th for Hobbit, Half-Elf and Elf; the spell list deltas - Detect Poison and Disease at 30 feet, Detect Phase for 6 turns, Cure Blindness and Lycanthropy, Energy, Wake Spell, Cure Insanity and Paralysis, Longevity at 10 game-years, Teleport and Size Control, Sterilize to 5 hit die, Neutralize Gas, Remove Charm at 3 inches, Cure Deafness, Improved Cure Serious Wounds at 4d6+1 per die for 8 to 24, Talk to Plants, Speak with Animals and Monsters. Mumper's Scribe: the curse on magical writing (permanent, incurable insanity for any but the counter-spell-knowing Scribe, Remove Curse notwithstanding), the two vocations, the 10-percent-a-week cumulative find chance, the specialist hire rate of 100-600 gold a week and the 1000-5000 gold a month fee, the six-grade ability ladder with the mistake percents within and above abilities and the above-abilities insanity, the alignment bands by vocation pinned as scanned with the sentinel for the clerical missing neutral band, the 100-percent mistake of the insane Scribe detectable only by ESP, the alignment mismatch multipliers of two and three, the 5-spells-by-2-points growth, the 5-percent cumulative monthly leave chance, and the uncorrectable mistakes at referee discretion. HONEST BOUNDARIES: the alignment block and the mistake pairs ride as scanned, no figure pixels to check; both specialists ride the variant layer, NPC-recommended per the editor's caution.
